messages.content:
Decide whether each claim is supported by the reference text below.

The reference text is the merged document merged.md. Each claim is
shown prefixed with its claim id and a pipe.

Verdicts:
SUPPORTED - the reference text states this claim, or states it in different
  words with the same meaning
CONTRADICTED - the reference text states something incompatible with this claim
MISSING - the reference text neither states nor contradicts this claim

Rules:
- Judge only against the reference text. Ignore outside knowledge.
- Different wording with identical meaning is SUPPORTED.
- A different value, number, unit or name for the same attribute is
  CONTRADICTED, not MISSING.
- Attribution still counts as stating the claim. If the reference text says
  that a named document states P, a claim of P is SUPPORTED.
- If the reference text gives several attributed values for one attribute, and
  this claim is one of them, the claim is SUPPORTED. Sources disagreeing with
  each other does not make either claim CONTRADICTED. Report the verdict for
  the claim in front of you and leave the disagreement to be recorded as a
  conflict.
- Partial support is MISSING. Do not extend the claim to make it fit.

Output:
- Return exactly one result per claim, in the order the claims are given, each
  echoing the claim id it answers. Never merge, reorder or omit a claim.
- Emit the fields in this order: verdict, evidence, evidence_source, rationale.
- verdict: commit to the verdict first, then explain it. The verdict must never
  be changed to fit the space available for the rationale.
- evidence: for SUPPORTED, the exact span of the reference text that states the
  claim. For CONTRADICTED, the exact span that is incompatible with it. Empty
  for MISSING.
- Copy every span character for character, including any spelling, grammatical
  or formatting errors, unusual capitalisation, and the original number, date
  and time formats. Do not correct, normalise, expand or abbreviate. A single
  altered character makes the evidence invalid.
- evidence_source: the filename the span was copied from. For this pass that is
  always merged.md.
- rationale: one sentence, maximum 400 characters, ending in a full stop. If
  your reasoning does not fit, shorten the rationale until it does. A rationale
  that stops mid-sentence is rejected, so do not work through the alternatives
  and let the space run out. Never drop it and never let it alter the verdict.

Worked example - attributed values on both sides of a conflict.

Suppose the reference text contains:

  Unresolved: default cache size.
  According to the Operator Guide, the default cache size is 64 MB.
  According to the Deployment Notes, the default cache size is 128 MB.
  The sources disagree and this merge does not choose between them.

Then "The default cache size is 64 MB." is SUPPORTED, with evidence "the
default cache size is 64 MB". "The default cache size is 128 MB." is also
SUPPORTED, with evidence "the default cache size is 128 MB". Neither is
CONTRADICTED: the reference text states both.

Quote the attributed value your claim matches. Never quote the sentence saying
that the sources disagree - that sentence is evidence for neither claim.

Worked example - verbatim evidence.

Suppose the reference text contains:

  The relay ran for tree days without a restart, from 07:15 till 19:45 daily.

For the claim "The relay ran for three days without a restart.", the evidence
is "The relay ran for tree days without a restart" - the misspelling "tree" is
preserved exactly as it appears. Writing "three" makes the evidence invalid.

For the claim "The relay ran from 07:15 till 19:45 daily.", the evidence is
"from 07:15 till 19:45 daily". Writing "from 7:15 am to 7:45 pm" makes the
evidence invalid.

Return JSON matching the provided schema. Nothing else.

REFERENCE TEXT (merged.md):
The pretty Rosegarden

Once upon a time, there was a princess in a distant country that loved to spend time in her beautiful rosegarden.

## Times

She visited the rosegarden every morning from 8 am till 9 am, right after her breakfast. From 02:00 till 15:30 o'clock, she worked in the rosegarden to tidy it up. Her mother did not appreciate that she, as a princess, would actually work in the garden, but the princess didn't care.

## Winter

The rosegarden lost all his life in winter, so the young lady could not enjoy the beautiful colors and all the life the rosegarden harbored. But once spring arrived, it turned back to life and color.

## Public times

While the rose garden was the private property of the royal family, the young princess insisted on making the garden accessible to the public every March 1st to March 31st. During that time, people from all over the country traveled to the castel to enjoy a nice day wandering through the rosegarden just like their beloved princess.

## Postcards

It became tradition that everyone who visited the rosegarden from the outside picked their favorite scenery and tried to draw what they liked most. They then sent the postcard to their home. People were starting to make bets on whether the postcard arrived at their home before they arrived home. In many cases, it was a tie because the people and the postcards were usually transported in the same carriage.

The creepy forest

Once upon a time there was an old lady that lived in a dark, spooky forest.

## Seasons

The forest was not traversable between October and April as it was too wet and too cold. The old lady nevertheless lived the entire year in the forest. Over the years, she acclimated to the weather and built strategies to survive the harsh conditions.

## Work

While many people suspected the old lady would be a witch that worked on forbidden magic, the reality was less exciting. Instead of harvesting skulls and bones, she collected wild herbs. Those wild herbs were tried and sold to wandering travelers who transported and sold the herbs into the cities.

## Illness

In one harsh winter, many people of the nearby village became very sick. In a desperate attempt to help the villagers, one young man took the courage and traveled to the old lady's house deep in the woods. It took him days to reach her house as he struggled with the wet and slippery ground. He also lost his orientation several times. But eventually, he reached her house. He carefully knocked and hoped that all the rumors about the lady were untrue. When she opened the door and saw the young man, she asked him to come into her house, sit at the fire and drink some hot soup she made for him.

## End

When the man recovered again, she gave him enough medicine made out of the herbs she collected in spring for the entire village. He traveled back to his village and went to the home of every sick person to provide them with the correct amount of medicine as told by the old lady from the woods. Eventually, everyone got healthy again and from then on the villagers sent a huge basket of cheese and dried meat to the old lady every autumn so that she could feast in winter.

CLAIMS:
a-visit-hours: The princess visited the rosegarden every morning from 8 am till 9 am.
a-work-hours-verbatim: The princess worked in the rosegarden from 02:00 till 15:30 o'clock.
a-winter-dormant: The rosegarden lost all its life in winter.
a-ownership: The rose garden was the private property of the royal family.
a-public-dates: The garden was accessible to the public every March 1st to March 31st.
a-postcard-tie: People and postcards were usually transported in the same carriage.
b-not-traversable: The forest was not traversable between October and April.
b-lady-year-round: The old lady lived in the forest the entire year.
b-herbs-not-magic: The old lady collected wild herbs rather than practising forbidden magic.
b-herbs-to-cities: Wandering travelers transported and sold the herbs into the cities.
b-medicine-village: She gave the man enough herb medicine for the entire village.
b-cheese-autumn: The villagers sent the old lady a basket of cheese and dried meat every autumn.
